canonicalExplanation.summary: Flexbox lays items out along one **main axis**, set by `flex-direction`: `row` (inline direction) or `column` (block direction). The other direction is the **cross axis**. `justify-content` distributes items along the **main** axis; `align-items` aligns them on the **cross** axis. So in a column, justify-content is vertical. Item sizing comes from `flex: grow shrink basis` — e.g. `flex: 1 1 12rem`.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
You turn a sidebar into `flex-direction: column` and use `justify-content: center` to center the buttons horizontally — and they jump to the vertical middle instead! The axes swapped. A column flex container uses justify-content for vertical distribution and align-items for horizontal cross-axis alignment. In this lesson you'll implement and explain a resilient one-dimensional component layout.

```predict
{"question": "In `display: flex; flex-direction: column;`, which property centers items horizontally?", "options": ["justify-content: center", "align-items: center"], "answer": 1, "why": "In a column, the main axis is vertical, so horizontal is the cross axis → align-items."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know **Normal flow and display** and **Intrinsic sizing and constraints** — flex items still have min-content minimums.

sections.heading: The model: main axis vs cross axis
sections.body:
| flex-direction | Main axis | justify-content moves items | align-items moves items |
|---|---|---|---|
| `row` (default). | horizontal (in LTR). | left–right. | up–down. |
| `column`. | vertical. | up–down. | left–right. |

```css
.toolbar { display: flex; gap: 0.5rem; align-items: center; }
.toolbar__search { flex: 1 1 12rem; min-width: 0; }  /* grow, shrink, start at 12rem */

.sidebar { display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; min-height: 100vh; }
```

| flex shorthand | Means |
|---|---|
| `flex: 1`. | grow 1, shrink 1, basis 0. |
| `flex: none`. | don't grow or shrink. |
| `flex: 1 1 12rem`. | start at 12rem, then grow/shrink. |

```reveal
{"prompt": "What does `gap` do in a flex container?", "answer": "It adds space between items (not at the outer edges), replacing margin hacks."}
```

sections.heading: Resilient sizing

includes: Identify main and cross axes for row and column flex containers.
Use justify-content, align-items, gap, flex and wrapping for resilient one-dimensional layouts.
excludes: Alignment of individual items and order (next lesson).

outcomes: Implement and explain a resilient one-dimensional component layout.

examples.title: Centering in a column
examples.situation: A column flex container uses justify-content for vertical distribution and align-items for horizontal cross-axis alignment.
walkthrough: **Column container:** `.sidebar { display: flex; flex-direction: column; }` — main axis is vertical.
**Vertical distribution:** `justify-content: space-between` puts the nav at the top and the account button at the bottom.
**Horizontal cross-axis alignment:** `align-items: center` centers the buttons left–right; the browser will render them centered in the sidebar.
examples.result: The sidebar spreads its groups vertically and centers them horizontally, as intended.

examples.title: The toolbar that overflowed
examples.situation: `.toolbar { display: flex }` holds a search input with `width: 300px` and three buttons. On a 320px phone it overflows.
walkthrough: The fixed 300px width plus buttons exceeds the container.
Flex items don't wrap by default.
Fix: `flex-wrap: wrap`, search `flex: 1 1 12rem; min-width: 0`, remove the fixed width.
examples.result: The toolbar fits on phones by shrinking and wrapping, and stretches on wide screens.

misconceptions.correction: justify-content controls the main axis, which depends on flex-direction. In a column container the main axis is vertical, so justify-content distributes items vertically and align-items handles horizontal alignment.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "Centering in a column", which property centered the buttons horizontally?

analogy.example: Flexbox is like **beads on a string**: the string's direction is the main axis. justify-content slides beads along the string; align-items moves them up or down off it. Turn the string vertical (column) and the moves swap.
limitations: Beads don't grow; flex items can.
Wrapping is like starting a second string.

steps.explanation: A column flex container makes the main axis vertical.
In this column, justify-content handles the vertical distribution.
In this column, align-items handles the horizontal cross-axis alignment.

trace.textAlternative: Aligning items in a column flex container. Step 1, Axes: main is vertical; cross is horizontal. A column flex container makes the main axis vertical. Step 2, Main axis: justify-content is space-between; effect is top and bottom groups. In this column, justify-content handles the vertical distribution. Step 3, Cross axis: align-items is center; effect is centered left–right. In this column, align-items handles the horizontal cross-axis alignment.

recap.summary: To implement a resilient one-dimensional layout, set flex-direction to define the main axis, use justify-content along it and align-items across it, space items with gap, and size items with flexible basis, min-width: 0 and wrapping instead of fixed widths.
